text:
Alyssa: seeing weird oscillation in p99 during short bursts this morning — looks like a repeating pattern every ~20s after scale-up. p95 mostly fine, but p99 jumps by ~3x for a minute then recovers.
Marc: can you paste the trace/heatmap?
Alyssa: pasted below, note kernel switch events and KV miss spikes.
Alyssa: kernel_events: SEEK->FAST_ATT->FALLBACK at 11:02:10, 11:02:31, 11:02:52; each time p99 spikes to ~920ms (normally ~320ms). KV cache hit% drops 98->60 then bounces.
Sophia: that smells like handshake/runner warmup + microbatch sizing mismatch. If kernel selector flips to FAST_ATT without KV primed it will cause extra memory ops.
Devon: also check probe sample sizes — our prober might be mis-classifying short-lived surges as steady state and flipping kernels too quickly.
Alyssa: here's a snippet from the prober log: "prober.sample_size=8, window=12s, smoothing_alpha=0.3"
Alyssa: and the autoscaler did a +2 GPU scale at 11:02:05 then another +1 at 11:02:28 (scaleup lag ~18s for the second pod).
Marc: oh that's the pattern — first scale brings capacity, traffic funnels and we hit a kernel choice boundary; second scale causes hot-swapping kernels while KV cache still cold on new workers -> tail.
Chiara: proposed quick mitigations: 1) increase prober.window to 30s, 2) add kernel-hysteresis to require stable deltas for 2 windows, 3) soft-prewarm new workers (KV prefetch) when scale detected.
Sophia: agree. Also tune microbatch target down for the short-burst route (e.g., target 2->1 microbatch for p99-sensitive routes) so fewer requests wait for batching and less kernel churn.
Devon: can we test a config locally? Suggest this patch to the prober:
Devon: ```
prober.window_seconds = 30
prober.min_samples = 16
kernel.selector.hysteresis_windows = 2
autoscaler.on_scaleup = prewarm_kv(true, timeout=8s)
```
Marc: nice. If prewarm_kv is enabled we need to watch cost; maybe conditional only for high-SLO routes.
Alyssa: ran a short canary with prewarm on the staging cluster for 30m: p99 tail reduced from 880ms->340ms during bursts, KV hit% steady at ~95% on new nodes.
Alyssa: canary logs: "prewarm_kv took 3.4s avg, warmed_keys=1.9k per node"
Chiara: great signal. Next steps: roll prober tuning + kernel hysteresis to canary for 6 hours, enable prewarm for top-10 latency-sensitive routes behind a flag.
Sophia: we should also add a microbatch override on route-level configs so product teams can opt-in to lower throughputs for tight SLOs.
Marc: agree. Create a short playbook: detection -> flip flag -> monitor 30m -> roll. Keep autoscaler unchanged for now.
Devon: I'll open PR with the prober change + unit tests for the hysteresis logic.
Alyssa: filing an ops ticket to run a wider canary tomorrow morning, will attach graphs. Thanks all :thumbsup: 
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary deployment created (canary/prober-tune-2394) by Devon at 2394123720.
Marc: ping me once the canary hits prod traffic pattern, I'll watch SLO dashboards.
Chiara: also add a quick profiler trace capture when p99 > 700ms to narrow down if any kernel path is taking unexpected syscalls.
Alyssa: noted. I'll include the profiler hook in the canary.
Sophia: TL;DR: kernel selector too eager + KV cold on new nodes + scaleup lag -> repeating p99 spikes during multi-step scale. Mitigations: prober smoothing, kernel hysteresis, KV prewarm, microbatch overrides.
